## Overview

The top app bar is the header of a mobile screen. It holds four things:
- a leading back or close action
- a title, with an optional subtitle
- up to three trailing actions
- an optional text action, such as Done or Save

Typical MakeMyTrip uses:
- "Mumbai to Delhi" over "Sat, 12 Oct · 1 Adult" on flight results
- a hotel name that appears over the hero photo once the page scrolls
- "My Trips" as a large title on a top-level screen

It comes in three platforms:

- **Android** follows Material 3: a start-aligned title, a 64 bar, and 48 touch targets.
- **iOS Classic** is the solid iOS navigation bar: a centred title, a 44 bar, and a brand chevron with the previous screen name.
- **iOS Glass** follows the iOS 27 Liquid Glass bar. The bar has no fill at rest. Actions float in glass capsules: a round back button, and one grouped capsule for the trailing icons. Once content scrolls under the bar, the iOS 27 hard scroll edge applies: a flat band with a hairline under it.

**iOS Classic and iOS Glass are under test.** The losing option will be deleted, as with the Segmented control thumb styles.

Each bar has two sizes:

- **Small** is one row. It is the everyday bar for listing, detail and booking screens.
- **Large** adds a headline row under the actions, for top-level screens. It collapses to Small as the page scrolls, so a scrolled Large bar is a Small bar.

There are three surfaces:

- **Default** is the white bar. It is the default.
- **Inverse** is the dark bar, for dark promo and premium sections such as MMTBLACK. It reuses the Inverse roles from Button.
- **Media** floats over a hero photo. The bar has no fill and no title, and each action sits in a white circle so it reads on any image. Once content scrolls under it, the bar takes the Default look: a white fill, the title, plain actions and the divider.

**Scrolled** adds a hairline divider under the bar. At the top of the page there is none, so the white bar runs into a white page.

### When to use something else

| Situation | Use |
|---|---|
| Switching between sections of the same screen | [Tab](tab.md) under the bar |
| A filter or sort row under the bar | [Chip](chip.md) |
| A list of overflow actions behind More | [Menu](menu.md), opened from the More action |
| A search field in the header | Not covered yet. It waits for a Text field component |
| A bar pinned to the bottom with a price and a Book button | A sticky footer with `shadow.sticky-bottom`, not this component |

### Composition

- **Top app bar** (`911:727`) has four variant axes: Platform, Size, Surface and Scrolled, with 24 variants. The grid is sparse. Large exists only at the top of the page, with the Default or Inverse surface.
- **Top app bar / Action** (`908:5370`, constitutive) is the leading and trailing control. Type (Icon, Text, Back label) x Surface (Default, Inverse, Media) x State (Default, Pressed, Disabled) gives 24 variants. Back label is iOS Classic only, so it exists only on Default and Inverse. The bar nests and exposes it, so a designer sets its Icon, Label and State from the bar panel. It is not a public Icon Button.
- **Icons:** `Icon / arrow-back` (`906:28`, the Android back), `Icon / chevron-left` (`906:31`, the iOS back), `Icon / more-vert` (`906:40`), `Icon / more-horiz` (`906:37`), `Icon / favorite` (`906:34`) and `Icon / search` (`906:43`) were added to the Icons page with this component. They are Material Symbols Rounded at weight 300, like the rest of the set.

## Platforms

| | iOS Classic | iOS Glass | Android |
|---|---|---|---|
| Small bar height | 44 | 56 | 64 |
| Title | Centred | Centred | Start-aligned, 4 after the back target |
| Back | Brand chevron plus the previous screen name, such as Flights | A round glass button with a neutral chevron and no label | A neutral arrow |
| Trailing icons | 44 targets, no fill | Grouped in one glass capsule | 48 targets, no fill |
| Text action | Brand label, 44 tall | Its own glass capsule | Brand label, 48 tall |
| Pressed feedback | The label or chevron darkens; icons show the state layer | The state layer inside the capsule | The state layer, a ripple in code |
| Large | A 52 headline row, so the bar is 96 | The same row under the 56 bar, so 108 | A 56 headline row, so the bar is 120 |
| Scroll edge | Divider | iOS 27 hard edge: a flat white band plus the divider | Divider |
| Base | `UINavigationBar` or SwiftUI `.toolbar` with a custom appearance: an opaque background, a hairline shadow on scroll | SwiftUI `.toolbar` on the iOS 27 SDK, which draws the glass. Keep `.scrollEdgeEffectStyle(.hard)`, the iOS 27 default | Material 3 `TopAppBar` and `LargeTopAppBar`, with Cosmos tokens replacing the Material colours and sizes |

The status bar and the safe area belong to the screen, not the component, so the bar starts below them. In the examples, iOS screens use a 54 status bar and Android a 24 one.

## API

| Property | Type | Values | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `platform` | enum | android \| iosClassic \| iosGlass | per platform | Code picks this from the platform; it is a Figma axis for mocks. |
| `size` | enum | small \| large | `small` | Large collapses to Small on scroll. |
| `surface` | enum | default \| inverse \| media | `default` | Media needs content with a hero image under the bar. |
| `title` | string | (string) | – | Required, even when hidden (Media at rest), because it is the screen name for assistive tech. One line, truncated with an ellipsis. |
| `subtitle` | string | (string) | none | Optional. One line, truncated. Use it for search context, not for a second title. |
| `leading` | `{ kind: back \| close \| none, label?, onAction }` | – | `back` | `label` is the iOS Classic back label, such as Flights. Drop it when it would crowd the title. |
| `actions` | `{ icon, label, onAction, disabled? }[]` | 0 to 3 | `[]` | Icon actions in order. The last can be More, which opens a Menu. |
| `textAction` | `{ label, onAction, disabled? }` | – | none | A short verb such as Done, Save or Edit. With a text action, `actions` holds at most two. |
| `scrolled` | boolean | true \| false | `false` | Driven by the scroll position in code. True once content passes under the bar. |

### Figma-only properties

| Figma property | Type | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Platform` | VARIANT | Android | Android, iOS Classic, iOS Glass. |
| `Size` | VARIANT | Small | Small or Large. Large only at Scrolled False, with Default or Inverse. |
| `Surface` | VARIANT | Default | Default, Inverse or Media. |
| `Scrolled` | VARIANT | False | True adds the divider. Media at True takes the Default look. |
| `Title`, `Subtitle` | TEXT | `"Title"`, `"Subtitle"` | One property drives both the Small title and the Large headline. |
| `Show leading` | BOOLEAN | `true` | Turn it off on top-level screens. |
| `Show subtitle` | BOOLEAN | `false` | |
| `Show action 1`, `Show action 2` | BOOLEAN | `true` | |
| `Show action 3` | BOOLEAN | `false` | Its default glyph is More: more-vert on Android, more-horiz on iOS. |
| `Show text action` | BOOLEAN | `false` | With it on, turn off at least one icon action. Figma cannot enforce this. |
| `Leading action`, `Action 1` to `Action 3`, `Text action` | Nested instance | exposed | Set their `Icon`, `Label`, `Back label` and `State` from the bar panel. |

Top app bar / Action has three variant axes and three text or swap properties:
- `Type`: Icon, Text or Back label
- `Surface`: Default, Inverse or Media
- `State`: Default, Pressed or Disabled
- an `Icon` swap
- a `Label` text for Text actions
- a `Back label` text for the iOS back button

State is design-only. In code, the platform draws pressed feedback. There are no Hover or Focus variants, because this is a touch component. A hardware keyboard focus ring comes from the platform.

Every variant ships placeholder copy. Realistic copy lives in the `Top app bar examples` frame (`913:305`).

## Behaviour

- **Scroll.**
  - Small: the divider appears as soon as content passes under the bar.
  - Large: the headline scrolls away with the content. On iOS, the centred Small title fades in once the headline passes under the bar. On Android, the bar shrinks to Small.
  - Media: at the first scroll, the bar takes the Default look, and the title fades in.
  - iOS Glass: the hard scroll edge appears.
- **Title.** One line. On Android it fills the space between the leading and trailing actions. On iOS it stays centred, and it truncates before it can touch either side, keeping at least `gap-title` clear. The subtitle truncates the same way. Shorten the copy rather than relying on truncation.
- **Text action rule.** A text action takes the room of one icon. With it on, show at most two icon actions. Put any further actions behind More.
- **More.** Overflow actions go in a Menu opened from the last action (more-vert on Android, more-horiz on iOS).
- **Back.** On iOS Classic the label is the previous screen name, shortened to Back when the title needs the room, and dropped when even that does not fit. Android and iOS Glass show the glyph only.
- **Disabled.** Disable a text action such as Save until the form is valid, rather than hiding it. Icon actions are rarely disabled; hide an action that does not apply.
- **Font scaling.** The Small bar keeps its height, and the title truncates. The Large headline grows with Dynamic Type and Android font scaling, and the bar grows with it.
- **Right-to-left.** The layout mirrors. The back glyphs flip; the share and more glyphs do not.

## Structure

### Anatomy

```
Top app bar
├─ Row                       (height: ios-min-height, glass-min-height or android-min-height)
│  ├─ Leading                (Show leading)
│  │  └─ Leading action      (Top app bar / Action; iOS Glass wraps it in a Back capsule)
│  ├─ Title                  (hidden on Large and on Media at rest)
│  │  ├─ Title               (title/medium/bold)
│  │  └─ Subtitle            (body/small/regular, Show subtitle)
│  └─ Trailing
│     ├─ Action 1 to 3       (Top app bar / Action, Show action n; iOS Glass groups them in one Capsule)
│     └─ Text action         (Top app bar / Action, Type Text, Show text action; its own Capsule on iOS Glass)
└─ Large title               (Large only)
   ├─ Large title            (headline/large/bold on iOS, headline/medium/bold on Android)
   └─ Large subtitle         (body/medium/regular, Show subtitle)
```

On iOS the Leading and Trailing frames share the leftover width equally, which keeps the title centred. On Android the title takes the leftover width.

## Color

Token names follow `top-app-bar/{part}-{surface}-{state}`, leaving Default out of the name, as Button does.

| Element | Default | Inverse | Media |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bar fill | `bg-default` → `bg-surface-secondary` #FFFFFF | `bg-inverse` → `bg-surface-inverse` #0A0A0A | `bg-media` → `transparent` at rest; `bg-default` once scrolled |
| iOS Glass bar fill at rest | `bg-glass` → `transparent` | `bg-glass` → `transparent` | `bg-glass` → `transparent` |
| Divider (Scrolled) | `divider-default` → `border-secondary` #E5E5E5 | `divider-inverse` → `border-inverse` #262626 | `divider-default` |
| Title | `title-default` → `text-primary` #0A0A0A | `title-inverse` → `text-inverse` #FFFFFF | hidden at rest |
| Subtitle | `subtitle-default` → `text-secondary` #525252 | `subtitle-inverse` → `text-inverse-secondary` #A1A1A1 | hidden at rest |
| Icon | `icon-default` → `icon` #0A0A0A | `icon-inverse-default` → `icon-inverse` #FFFFFF | `icon-media-default` → `icon` #0A0A0A |
| Icon, Pressed | `icon-pressed` on `bg-pressed` → `bg-fill-pressed-strong` #E5E5E5 | `icon-inverse-pressed` on `bg-inverse-pressed` → `bg-fill` #FFFFFF at `bg-opacity-inverse-pressed` (10%) | `icon-media-pressed` on `bg-media-pressed` → `bg-surface-secondary-pressed` #F5F5F5 |
| Icon, Disabled | `icon-disabled` → `icon-disabled` #A1A1A1 | `icon-inverse-disabled` → `icon-inverse-disabled` #737373 | `icon-disabled` |
| Media circle and pill | – | – | `bg-media-default` → `bg-surface-secondary` #FFFFFF, with `media-circle-shadow` → `shadow.card-subtle` |
| Text action | `label-text-default` → `text-brand` #0067E8 | `label-text-inverse-default` → `text-brand-inverse` #83D4FF | `label-text-default` |
| Text action, Pressed | `label-text-pressed` → `text-brand-pressed` #0857C5 on `bg-text-pressed` → `bg-fill-pressed-strong` | `label-text-inverse-pressed` → `text-brand-inverse-pressed` #D6EFFF on `bg-text-inverse-pressed` at 10% | `label-text-pressed` on `bg-media-pressed` |
| Text action, Disabled | `label-text-disabled` → `text-disabled` #A1A1A1 | `label-text-inverse-disabled` → `text-inverse-disabled` #737373 | `label-text-disabled` |
| iOS Classic back chevron and label | `icon-back-default`, `label-back-default` → brand #0067E8; Pressed #0857C5 | `icon-back-inverse-default`, `label-back-inverse-default` → #83D4FF; Pressed #D6EFFF | Media uses a chevron in a white circle instead |

The iOS Glass capsules use these tokens:
- **Fill.** `capsule-bg` (→ `bg-surface-secondary`, #FFFFFF) at `capsule-bg-opacity` (75%).
- **Edge.** `capsule-border` (→ `border-secondary`).
- **Shadow.** `capsule-shadow` (→ `shadow.card-subtle`).
- **On an Inverse bar.** `capsule-bg-inverse` (→ `bg-surface-inverse`) at `capsule-bg-opacity-inverse` (75%), with `capsule-border-inverse` (→ `border-inverse`).
- **Actions inside.** They take the Default or Inverse action colours.

This component adds no semantic roles.

| Default: subtitle #525252 on #FFFFFF | 7.81:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Default: text action and iOS back #0067E8 on #FFFFFF | 5.12:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Default: icon Pressed #0A0A0A on #E5E5E5 | 15.72:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Default: text action Pressed #0857C5 on #E5E5E5 | 5.24:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Inverse: title and icons #FFFFFF on #0A0A0A | 19.80:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Inverse: subtitle #A1A1A1 on #0A0A0A | 7.66:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Inverse: text action and back #83D4FF on #0A0A0A | 12.09:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Inverse: icon Pressed #FFFFFF on the 10% white layer (#232323) | 15.72:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Inverse: text action Pressed #D6EFFF on #232323 | 13.21:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Media: icon #0A0A0A on its white circle / Pressed #F5F5F5 | 19.80 / 18.16:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Media: text action #0067E8 on its white pill / Pressed #0857C5 on #F5F5F5 | 5.12 / 6.06:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Media: white circle on a photo | Depends on the photo | 3:1 | Shadow-backed; on a near-white photo the circle relies on `shadow.card-subtle` |
| Glass: icon #0A0A0A on the 75% white capsule over a white / grey / black backdrop | 19.80 / 19.46 / 11.11:1 | 3:1 | Pass |
| Glass: text action #0067E8 on the capsule over white / grey / black | 5.12 / 5.03 / 2.87:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass on light content; fails over very dark content (see Known gaps) |
| Glass Inverse: icon #FFFFFF / text action #83D4FF on the 75% dark capsule over white | 9.29 / 5.67:1 | 4.5:1 | Pass |
| Divider #E5E5E5 on #FFFFFF / #262626 on #0A0A0A | 1.26 / 1.31:1 | – | Decorative. The bar edge is not a control boundary |

The linter checks the title, subtitle, label and icon keys for Default, Inverse and Media on every build (`tokens/contrast`). It does not check the Glass capsule figures; they were computed by hand from the 75% blend.

### Semantics

| | iOS / VoiceOver | Android / TalkBack |
|---|---|---|
| Title | The navigation title; VoiceOver reads it as a header (`.isHeader`). On Media at rest the title is not drawn but still names the screen | `Modifier.semantics { heading() }` on the title. On Media at rest the screen name comes from `paneTitle` |
| Back | "Back, button", or "Flights, back button" when a label shows. The escape gesture also goes back | `contentDescription = "Navigate up"` (Material default) or "Back". System Back does the same |
| Close | "Close, button" | `contentDescription = "Close"` |
| Icon actions | Each needs a name: "Share", "Add to shortlist", "More options". A toggle such as shortlist also reports its state (`.isSelected`) | `contentDescription` on each, with `Role.Button`; a toggle reports `toggleableState` |
| Text action | The label is the name; disabled reads "dimmed" | The label is the name; disabled reads "disabled" |
| Order | Back, title, actions in visual order, text action last | The same |
| Hit area | 44 x 44 pt, even inside the 36 Media circle | 48 x 48 dp, even inside the 36 Media circle |

A long-press on an icon action shows its name. On Android this is a Plain [Tooltip](tooltip.md); on iOS it is the system large content viewer at large text sizes.

## Platform mapping

| | iOS (SwiftUI) | Android (Compose) |
|---|---|---|
| Bar fill | `.toolbarBackground(CosmosTokens.topAppBarBgDefault, for: .navigationBar)` (Classic) | `colors = TopAppBarDefaults.topAppBarColors(containerColor = CosmosTokens.topAppBarBgDefault)` |
| Title | `.navigationTitle` with `.toolbarTitleDisplayMode(.inline)` for Small and `.large` for Large | `TopAppBar(title = …)`, `LargeTopAppBar(title = …)` with `TopAppBarDefaults.exitUntilCollapsedScrollBehavior()` |
| Scrolled divider | The bar shadow colour set to `topAppBarDividerDefault` (Classic); the hard scroll edge (Glass) | A 1 dp `HorizontalDivider(color = CosmosTokens.topAppBarDividerDefault)` shown when `scrollBehavior.state.overlappedFraction > 0` |
| Actions | `ToolbarItem(placement: .topBarTrailing)`; on Glass, items in one `ToolbarItemGroup` share a capsule | `actions = { IconButton(…) }`, sized `CosmosTokens.topAppBarAndroidTargetSize` |
| Media | A transparent bar over the hero, with each action in a `Circle()` of `topAppBarMediaCircleSize` | `containerColor = Color.Transparent` until the scroll offset passes the hero |

```css
/* Web views inside the apps */
.top-app-bar {
  background: var(--top-app-bar-bg-default);
  min-height: var(--top-app-bar-android-min-height);
  padding-inline: var(--top-app-bar-android-padding-x);
}
.top-app-bar[data-scrolled="true"] {
  border-bottom: var(--top-app-bar-divider-width) solid var(--top-app-bar-divider-default);
}
.top-app-bar__action {
  inline-size: var(--top-app-bar-android-target-size);
  block-size: var(--top-app-bar-android-target-size);
  border-radius: var(--top-app-bar-action-radius);
  color: var(--top-app-bar-icon-default);
}
```

## Known gaps

- **Classic versus Glass under test.** If Glass wins, delete the iOS Classic variants, the Back label actions and the `label-back-*`, `icon-back-*`, `ios-min-height`, `ios-padding-x`, `ios-text-padding-x` and `back-gap` tokens. Keep `ios-target-size` and the large title tokens. If Classic wins, delete the iOS Glass variants and every `capsule-*`, `glass-*` and `bg-glass` token.
- **Glass is approximated.** Figma draws the glass as a 75% white fill with a background blur and a hairline edge. The real iOS 27 material refracts and tints, adapts to the content under it, and follows the transparency slider, Reduce Transparency and Increase Contrast. Blur and refraction cannot be tokens. Code uses the system glass and keeps the tokens for colours and sizes only.
- **Brand text on light glass over dark content.** A light capsule over a very dark photo blends to about #C2C2C2, where `text-brand` falls to 2.87:1. iOS adapts the glass to dark content, so this is a Figma-only worst case. Over dark sections, use the Inverse surface.
- **Media over bright photos.** The white circle can sit on a near-white photo. The `shadow.card-subtle` lift carries its edge there.
- **Title truncation in Figma.** Figma lets the title hug, so long placeholder copy can push actions aside in a mock. In code the title truncates.
- **Sparse grid.** Large has no Scrolled or Media variants. Switching a Large bar to one of those in Figma shows a missing-variant warning; switch Size to Small first.
- **Capsule with every icon hidden.** On iOS Glass, turning off all three icon actions leaves an empty capsule visible. Figma booleans cannot hide a parent when all its children are off.
- **No motion tokens.** The collapse, title fade and divider fade use the platform defaults.
- **No search bar.** A header search field waits for a Text field component.
- **Not uSpec-generated.** This file is hand-authored next to the Figma build.

`ios-min-height`, `ios-target-size` and `capsule-size` alias the primitive `spacing.44`, and `glass-min-height` aliases `spacing.56`, because no `space.*` step holds 44 or 56.

Platform names follow the standard pipeline: `top-app-bar/bg-default` → `--top-app-bar-bg-default` (CSS) → `CosmosTokens.topAppBarBgDefault` (Swift and Kotlin) → `tokens["top-app-bar"]["bg-default"]` (TS).

### Figma

- Page `Top app bar` (`908:2`): Docs `912:767`, showcase `Top app bars` (`912:305`) with its Grid Legend (`912:312`), showcase `Actions` (`909:17`) with its Grid Legend (`909:21`), and `Top app bar examples` (`913:305`).
- The showcases put Media rows on a photo-like gradient band and iOS Glass Inverse rows on a dark band, because those bars have no fill of their own. The bands are locked decoration, bound to `exp-blue-400`, `exp-amber-300` and `bg-surface-inverse`.
- Grid Legend labels are written in JetBrains Mono Medium; switch them to SF Mono Medium.
